node_labels: piSignage web application player API path traversal in versions before 2.6.4. A remote attacker authenticated as a low-privilege user can request api/settings/log?file=../ and download arbitrary files from the underlying Raspberry Pi.
Oculus Browser arbitrary HTML injection affecting the browser user interface from version 5.2.7 through 5.7.11. A remote web page can inject attacker-controlled HTML into the Oculus Browser UI.

Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe privileged arbitrary-file-write vulnerability before version 1.44.0.32849 on Windows. A privileged OVRRedir.exe process can be induced to write to an attacker-selected file through a hard link to a log file.

RaspAP 2.5 authenticated web-console command execution through includes/webconsole.php. The web console is misconfigured and virtually unrestricted, allowing commands against the underlying Raspberry Pi operating system.
Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher.exe handle-management vulnerability affecting versions after 1.39 and before 31.1.0.67.507. A privileged process handle can be exposed to an unprivileged process.

Raspberry Pi Glowworm side-channel attack affecting Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and Raspberry Pi 4 B devices through 2021-08-09 in specific audio-output use cases. The power indicator LED leaks information about sound played through connected speakers.
Raspberry Pi OS default credential exposure through version 5.10. The pi account retains the default password when the administrator has not changed it.
NVIDIA Jetson Linux IOMMU misconfiguration. An unprivileged attacker with physical access can use the PCI bus to obtain direct read/write access to the entire system address space.

edge_labels: Credential and privilege transition: successfully using the unchanged pi password provides administrator-level authenticated access on the Raspberry Pi. If RaspAP is deployed on that host and accepts the pi account or the same credentials, this satisfies the authenticated-access precondition for the virtually unrestricted includes/webconsole.php web console, after which the attacker can execute operating-system commands, upload files, and execute code.

Conditional credential-reuse transition: administrator-level access obtained with the unchanged pi password can satisfy the piSignage low-privilege authenticated-user precondition if the piSignage web application uses the pi account or reused credentials. The attacker can then invoke api/settings/log?file=../ to download arbitrary Raspberry Pi files.

Conditional file-disclosure transition: arbitrary files retrieved through the piSignage log-download path traversal may contain RaspAP configuration, authentication material, session data, or reused credentials. If such material provides authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5, the disclosed credentials satisfy the web-console precondition and enable command execution, file uploads, and code execution on the Raspberry Pi.
